current.text: He is a locked-in starter at forward. Tari Eason has not passed him on the depth chart.
His minutes are stable and higher than Alperen Sengun's. Coach Ime Udoka plays his starters very heavy minutes.
With Steven Adams back, he plays more power forward than center.
He is not a high-usage player on this team.
Lloyd sees no reason to expect more blocks, more steals or higher usage this season.
Experts call him too early in the 90s or inside the top 100. They see fair value around pick 115 or later, where he can deliver as a late pick.
He is a rock-solid pick with little upside.
With a March 28 end, the Rockets play 3-3-4 in the fantasy playoff weeks, 10 games over three weeks.
That fantasy playoff schedule is weak.
The Rockets have only 14 back-to-backs this season.
The Rockets are predicted to win 54 games.

durable.text: He is a 3-and-D role player who is around average in many areas. He will never be a star, and he is a boring fantasy pick.
His interior defense, rim deterrence and weak-side shot blocking have grown a lot. Smaller, quick guards can beat him on the perimeter.
He shot only about 35% on open and wide-open threes, which is below league average.
He needs to become a more reliable shooter.
He makes many threes for a forward or center.
His FG% is weak for his position.

note: At Yahoo rank 96 (5 USD value, 1.9 USD average cost) and ESPN rank 111 (1.5 USD average cost), he is a 1 to 3 USD late pick in our league, and he went for 1 USD in our last auction. The experts want him around pick 115, not in the 90s. He gives about 2.1 threes from the frontcourt on steady starter minutes and fits punt FG% builds best. Early in the season, check that his 35 minutes hold with Eason and Adams around and whether his three-point shooting improves. Remember the weak 10-game playoff schedule.
